rationale: First-stage spatial forecast-error borrowing did not transfer to Alaska. Those outcomes are retained. Second stage examines persistence and spatial breadth conditional on richer multiscale magnitude-specific rates.
status: Italy, Greece and Alaska are now development regions. The new Chile audit has not been downloaded or scored.

feature_blocks.ratebank: 33 trailing counts for three relative magnitude thresholds and 11 windows
feature_blocks.duration: active days and weeks, dominant day share, average age, older-half share, count dispersion, daily entropy
feature_blocks.spread: 4x4 occupied subcells, spatial entropy/dominance, depth spread, spatial covariance
feature_blocks.marks: smoothed tail fractions and mean/SD of relative magnitude

selection: 14 fixed learner configurations, 2010-2014 fit and 2015-2019 validation. Choose ONE additional-feature family among duration/spread/marks/persistence/joint by mean validation log-loss gain over ratebank across Italy/Greece/Alaska for primary target, before Chile scoring. Chile hyperparameters chosen on same historical split only.
chile: USGS 2000-2025, 46S-17S and 78W-66W, depth0-60km, minimum reported M4.5; 2deg cells anchored46S78W, pre2010 eligibility30 M4.5 and5 M5.0; primary5<=M<10 (reported magnitude upper10.0, equivalent normalized upper8.5), band5-6 andM>=6. Internally subtract1.5 from reported magnitude to use common ETAS Mc3.0; catalog keeps original magnitudes.
evaluation: Primary fixed2019 calibration and annual update sensitivity. 2020-2025 audit only once family/code frozen. Baselines calibratedETAS, adaptiveblend, multiscale ratebank, selected best no-extra-feature, and matched ratebank. Holm across3Chile targets. Further new feature searches would require another external cohort and be disclosed.
interpretation: Observational forecasting skill conditional on regional temporal ETAS; no physical precursor or prospective claim.
pre_acquisition_correction: Corrected the upper-magnitude wording to match normalized ETAS support; retain the 2010 M8.8 mainshock.
